name: application-dependency-link-row
title: Dependency Link Row
description: Two-group relationship panel showing which issues an item blocks and which block it, each as a row of linked chips carrying a status-colored dot.
useWhen: An issue-tracker or project-management detail view needs to surface blocking relationships between items.
Users need to jump directly to a related issue, not just see that a relationship exists.
The relationship has a clear direction (this blocks that, or is blocked by that) worth labeling separately.
avoidWhen: The relationship is symmetric with no direction (e.g. 'related to') — a single unlabeled chip row is simpler.
There are no dependencies to show — omit the panel entirely rather than rendering an empty state for it.
You need to visualize many interlinked dependencies at once — use a dependency graph or org-chart-style diagram instead of stacked rows.
responsiveBehavior: The panel is a fixed max-w-md card whose chip rows wrap naturally to fill the available width at any viewport size.
accessibility: Each group has a heading combining an icon and a count ('Blocks 2 issues'), so the relationship type and quantity are both announced as text.
Status dots on each chip are aria-hidden since they're supplementary to the issue ID, which is always visible text.
Each chip is a real link, so the underlying issue is reachable and activatable by keyboard.

variants.title: Dependency link row
variants.description: Two groups: 'Blocks 2 issues' and 'Blocked by 1 issue', each with linked issue-ID chips and a status dot.
accessibility: Group headings pair a directional icon with text so the relationship reads correctly even without color.

variants.title: Dependency link row (Dark)
variants.description: Dependency link row adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Chip border, background, and status-dot colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
